 Tonight's Hunter's Moon will glow orange for a spooky October sky
 Astronomers say this October supermoon could deliver a "spooky" celestial display
 By Kyley Warren 
 Published on Oct. 25, 2026
 — Our editors and readers independently select what you see on USA TODAY 10BEST. When you buy through a link on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. A flock of crows flies past as the “Hunter's Moon” rises over Frankfurt, Germany, November 5, 2025. REUTERS/Kai Pfaffenbach – Photo courtesy of Kai Pfaffenbach, REUTERS 
 After an already-eventful celestial month, astronomers are forecasting tonight's skies could offer a spooky start to Halloween week — thanks to an orange October full moon, known as the Hunter's Moon, that's set to peak late tonight in some parts of the United States.
 Per NASA , a Hunter's Moon has historically been tied to seasonal traditions; the October super moon used to act as a signal for farmers that the fields were cleared from the autumn harvest, and also doubled as a light source for hunters who were beginning to track games for their winter food hauls.
 The lunar event is a particularly special one, as it marks the first full moon after the Harvest Moon , and the closet full moon to the beginning of the autumn equinox.

 Peak date: Monday, Oct. 26, 2026
 Peak time: 12:12 a.m. EDT (late Sunday night, Oct. 25, in Western time zones)
 Visibility forecast: Varies, but is forecasted to be excellent in most parts of the United States
 What you need to see tonight's Hunter's Moon
 Astronomers predict tonight's Hunter's Moon — one of fall 2026's most spectacular celestial events — will be visible with just the naked eye (dependent on sky conditions and visibility, of course).
 But select sky-watching essentials can be helpful to ensure you get the best view of the October full moon, like a telescope or binoculars; I've linked out a few of my favorite skywatching products below.

 The 2026 Hunter's Moon will peak early tomorrow morning, Oct. 26, just after midnight in Eastern time zones; for Western time zones, it will reach maximum brightness before midnight tonight, Oct. 25, closer to 9 p.m. PST.
 During this time, skywatchers can see the super moon at its brightest and largest, with a vibrant orange hue emitting from it. This October astronomical event marks the first full moon that follows the Harvest Moon and is also closest to the beginning of the autumn equinox.
 More Hunter's Moon skywatching tips:
 For a better sky-watching experience, use these tips to guide your Hunter's Moon viewing tonight or early tomorrow morning:
 Get away from light pollution : If you can trek to a dark-sky spot or at least an area with minimal light pollution, you'll have a much better view of the night sky.
 Avoid phone screens : Give your eyes minimum 20 minutes to adjust to the dark skies, keeping bright screens and distractions at bay.
